Claude responded: I added the program and speakers pages to the site, but the speaker photos and bios are placeholders because the workbook doesn't contain any.

Ran 6 commands, read memory, and 3 more tools

I added the program and speakers pages to the site, but the speaker photos and bios are placeholders because the workbook doesn’t contain any. The Speaker Bios sheet only has grey “PHOTO (insert here)” boxes and “Biography to be announced” for everyone. I didn’t write bios myself, since I’d be guessing about real people. I haven’t been able to render the site in Quarto (it isn’t installed here), only check the pages with pandoc.

What’s in the package

  • program.qmd: one tab per day (Wed 2 Dec, Thu 3 Dec, Fri 4 Dec), with the full timetable (opening, panels, breaks, dinner, closing). Each parallel block shows its 5 sessions as cards, with chair, paper titles and authors (presenter in bold), and the thesis workshop sessions marked with a badge. It covers all 100 papers in 25 sessions.
  • speakers.qmd: a card for each of the 8 named speakers with photo, affiliation, conference role and bio. Names in the program link to their cards.
  • index.qmd: the dates now read December 2–4 (they said 3–4, but your program starts on 2 Dec). The “Keynote Speakers: TBA” section is replaced with Program and Speakers buttons.
  • assets/program.css: styling, using a green/gold fallback palette since I don’t have your site theme.
  • build_program.py: regenerates both pages from the workbook.

To add photos and bios

  1. Put photos in images/speakers/ named like ratha-chiv.jpg (the build script prints the exact names). Until a photo is there, the card shows the speaker’s initials.
  2. Fill the Bio column on the workbook’s Speakers sheet, then run python build_program.py SAERD26_Program_v6.xlsx.

You’ll also need to add program.qmd and speakers.qmd to your navbar in _quarto.yml, which I don’t have.

Worth checking in the workbook

  • B5 duplicate: B5 lists “Groundwater Depletion in Lahore” twice (slots 1 and 2, flagged as a possible duplicate in your Data sheet). I published it as submitted.
  • Day 3 overlap: the coffee break (10:00–10:30) overlaps Parallel D (08:30–10:30). I kept it as in the workbook.
  • Panel A: the speakers and moderator are still blank, so the page says “To be announced”.
  • “Micheal” Hill: the workbook spells it that way. It may be “Michael”.
  • Stale page content: the submission deadlines and the “Submit Your Abstract” buttons on the homepage are still live even though the dates have passed. I left them alone.

Files are in /mnt/user-data/outputs/:

  • saerd-site.zip

Claude responded: Adding a "Explore Siem Reap" section to the homepage now: Angkor Pass booking, top temples, food and fun activities.

Searched the web, ran 2 commands

Adding a “Explore Siem Reap” section to the homepage now: Angkor Pass booking, top temples, food and fun activities.

Ran a command, shared files

I added an “Explore Siem Reap” section to index.qmd, after the travel and accommodation section and before Contact. I only checked it with pandoc, not in Quarto, so check how it looks on the site.

The new section covers

  • Booking the Angkor Pass: buy only from the official operator, Angkor Enterprise, online at angkorenterprise.gov.kh or at its ticket office on Road 60. A table lists the three passes: 1-day $37, 3-day $62 (any 3 days within 7 days), and 7-day $72 (any 7 days within 30 days). It also covers photos for the 3-day and 7-day passes, buying after 5 PM for sunrise the next day, children under 12 entering free, the dress code (shoulders and knees covered), and opening hours.
  • Most important temples:
    • Angkor Wat, Bayon (Angkor Thom), Ta Prohm, Banteay Srei and Preah Khan, plus Phnom Bakheng or Pre Rup for sunset and Beng Mealea.
    • Each has a short reason to visit and a tip, and the section includes a one-day plan for the Small Circuit.
  • Food: fish amok, lok lak, Khmer red curry, nom banh chok, kuy teav, and local drinks. It also lists where to eat: Old Market, night markets, Pub Street, and the Wat Bo and Kandal Village areas.
  • Fun activities:
    • Phare, the Cambodian Circus, an Apsara dance dinner and the night markets.
    • Tonle Sap floating villages, a cooking class, the Cambodia Landmine Museum, the Angkor National Museum and Phnom Kulen.
    • Cycling or a tuk-tuk tour.

To double-check before you publish

  • Pass validity: sources disagree on whether the 3-day pass is valid for 7 or 10 days. I used 7 days, which matches the official pages as recently as October 2026. The section tells readers to confirm on the official site.
  • Dates for temple visits: the page suggests 1 and 5 December for temple visits. Change these if your program or free time differs.
  • Restaurants and shows: I named dishes, areas and attractions, but no specific restaurants or show times, because those change. Tell me if you want some added.

Replace index.qmd on your site. The zip has everything.
